headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared document workflows; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can use optional web search, so attacker-controlled content could enter its outputs. pdf.js renders PDF files in a browser-based worker, creating a plausible path where PDF content from B is fed into A or copied manually. No shared MCP or clipboard is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF pdf.js output or rendered PDF text is copied into Khoj prompts or indexed notes, injection becomes plausible.
IF Khoj ingests externally sourced notes that contain attacker-controlled instructions, those instructions can influence downstream responses.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted PDFs into Khoj.
Add a manual review step before indexing PDF-derived text.
Use a prompt delimiter/template that labels retrieved text as untrusted.
Restrict pdf.js to trusted documents only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from pdf.js into Khoj retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while pdf.js handles PDF files. If both are pointed at the same workspace or document set, sensitive content can flow from A into B’s rendered outputs or logs. Khoj’s broad network egress increases exposure if it sends retrieved context to external services; pdf.js itself has no egress, so the risk is bounded but real.
conditions: IF Khoj is configured to index documents that pdf.js also opens from the same folder, both agents see the same sensitive files.
IF Khoj forwards retrieved context to a cloud model provider, indexed notes may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate the folders used by Khoj and pdf.js.
Turn off cloud-backed retrieval for sensitive notes.
Review which PDFs are indexed before opening them in pdf.js.
Use local-only inference for Khoj when handling private documents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it, and pdf.js only reads PDF files in a browser-based worker. Because neither profile shows unrestricted write access to the same directory, there is no strong write-write conflict. The remaining overlap is read-only, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF either agent is wrapped with additional tooling that adds filesystem writes, the current assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts where possible.
Avoid sharing a mutable working directory.
Run pdf.js in a separate browser profile.
Document any added write-capable wrappers before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieval-based answers from indexed documents, and pdf.js can surface PDF text that may be treated as source material. If a user or orchestrator treats Khoj’s output as authoritative after pdf.js renders a document, errors can cascade into incorrect summaries or actions. No verification layer is documented between them, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF pdf.js-rendered text is pasted into Khoj and then reused without verification, errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on Khoj summaries of PDFs, a mistaken summary can cascade into a wrong action.
mitigations: Require source-link verification for any Khoj summary of a PDF.
Compare critical claims against the original PDF before acting.
Mark Khoj outputs as draft unless manually checked.
Limit downstream automation to non-sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving extraction from pdf.js into Khoj.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile shows a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Khoj handles personal notes and indexed documents, while pdf.js handles PDFs; absent a documented compliance gap, only a low residual risk remains from local handling practices. The other agent is cited because the assessment is pairwise, but no mismatch is evident.
conditions: IF Khoj is used with regulated personal data while pdf.js is deployed in an environment with stricter retention rules, a mismatch could emerge.
IF either agent is configured to retain documents beyond policy, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both tools.
Keep regulated data out of ad hoc PDF workflows.
Document where PDFs and notes are stored.
Review deletion/export procedures before use.
